raw.question: Split lifecycle migration out of PR #384 and reject destructive in-place transitions
raw.chosen: Split lifecycle migration out of PR #384 and reject destructive in-place transitions
raw.reasoning: The complete state model is enumerable only if the current PR refuses layout changes and scoped allowlist removals at the same local root. Additions preserve existing scope roots; unchanged/omitted configuration reuses persisted paths, layout, and cursor identity; removals or layout changes require a new LOCAL_DIR with --rehome. Historical-root retention is deferred until a real lifecycle use case defines drain semantics. Per-scope skip-stuck remains because it is correctness for the shipped command.

events.content: The third review round exposed one multi-root lifecycle blast radius rather than unrelated bugs. Narrowing to explicit refusal makes the allowed state transitions finite and reviewable; focused tests now pass for both refusal boundaries, exact-root reconstruction, cursor identity merge semantics, and per-scope skip-stuck.

raw.adjustments: Removed historical-root retention; reject in-place scope removal; preserve state identity and iterate active cursors

retrospective.summary: Narrowed PR #384 lifecycle behavior to explicit refusal: in-place layout changes and scoped allowlist removals require rehome; persisted mount state identity lets skip-stuck visit every active scope cursor. Removed historical-root migration, preserved exact remote roots, and added focused end-to-end/unit coverage. Full go test ./... -count=1, go vet ./..., and focused race suite pass.
